paragraphs.body: I thought back to my mom’s warning. She was right, I was close to the sun, but only because I was the best of the best. And maybe it was a long way down, but I would never know what the fall felt like.

annotations.comment: Waylon, you have this fascinating situation here, where a woman allllmost learns a lesson but then just doubles down on being a jerk. I wonder what happens to this story if she does actually learn the lesson — if this firing does actually break her — and then what happens? Maybe she goes back to her mom and apologizes? Maybe she tries to talk to the supervisor again? Or maybe she decides, nope, I did nothing wrong and I’ll apply elsewhere. (This is what you have now, except she never really changes or even seems like she might.) I do think you’ve at times gone beyond what makes logical sense — I couldn’t believe that a supervisor would fire his resident when she happened to wander into the hospital or that she could just apply elsewhere. So I would suggest thinking through that a bit, maybe trying to find someone’s online post about what happens when you get fired. I didn’t mind so much that I don’t much like Addie, but it was also hard to stay interested in her when she was a jerk to everyone. Is there anyone she’s nice to?Happy revising! Thanks!Grade: A
